alignments.note: Working analysis: opening temporal expression plus an existential/past construction and mltha. The capitalized Greek term and Hebrew definiteness are target editorial choices; no assertion of an ancient target original.

alignments.sy: ܘܗܘ ܡܠܬܐ ܐܝܬܘܗܝ ܗܘܐ ܠܘܬ ܐܠܗܐ

alignments.note: Working analysis: the repeated mltha is related to alha by lwth. Together-with is a proposed relational reading, not proof of a spatial or metaphysical account.

Working analysis: preserve the source-fronted divine term in the proposed target order. Predicate/subject identification and definiteness need Syriac and target review; source word order alone does not settle theology.

he.register: biblical-style Hebrew; new translation, not ancient original
he.text: הכל נהיה בידו ובלעדיו לא נהיה דבר אחד מכל אשר נהיה׃

alignments.el_proposed: Όλα ήρθαν στην ύπαρξη με το χέρι του
alignments.note: Working analysis: kl plus a hand-expression and hwa. Coming into existence is an interpretive contextual reading. Preserve hand language in the first draft; decide whether literal wording wrongly suggests a physical hand or, in Hebrew, mere possession.

alignments.el_proposed: και χωρίς αυτόν δεν ήρθε στην ύπαρξη ούτε ένα πράγμα
alignments.note: Working analysis: negative exception with one. Greek supplies a noun here and Hebrew places dbr here for idiomatic syntax; no second source noun is being claimed.

Working analysis: proposed dependent relative/partitive attachment to the negative clause. The target partitive and Hebrew kl are interpretive expansions, not separate Syriac words; reviewer may prefer less expansion or different attachment.

he.register: biblical-style Hebrew; new translation, not ancient original
he.text: בו היו חיים והחיים היו אור בני האדם׃

alignments.note: Working analysis: life with an in-him expression and hwa. Pronoun reference and whether in/by/through is intended require review. Hebrew plural agreement is target grammar, not a claim of multiple lives.

alignments.el_proposed: και η ζωή ήταν το φως των ανθρώπων
alignments.note: Working analysis: life identified with light for humanity. Greek anthropoi and Hebrew bnei ha-adam are proposed generic-human renderings, not a male-only restriction. Copular aspect/tense must be independently checked.

he.register: biblical-style Hebrew; new translation, not ancient original
he.text: והאור ההוא מאיר בחשך והחשך לא השיגו׃

alignments.el_proposed: Και εκείνο το φως λάμπει μέσα στο σκοτάδι
alignments.note: Working analysis: renewed reference to that light, darkness and a shining expression. Proposed present tense should be checked against the Syriac form and discourse.

alignments.el_proposed: και το σκοτάδι δεν το κυρίευσε
alignments.note: UNRESOLVED lexical/contextual choice. Greek currently proposes overpowering; Hebrew offers a less narrowed reach/overtake expression. These are not yet a semantically harmonized pair. Neither is asserted to exhaust the Syriac sense.
